headline: The Select Board authorized $12.5 million in regional dispatch borrowing, while multiple boards backed a joint Route 9 corridor study with Westborough.
synopsis: The Select Board voted 4-1 to approve up to $12.5 million in temporary bridge borrowing for the MetroWest Regional Emergency Communication Center and elected Kathy Cook as board chair. Multiple town boards, including the Select Board, Planning Board, and Wastewater Study Committee, endorsed a joint state grant application with Westborough for a $150,000 Route 9 corridor study. The Regional School Committee initially voted down its food service contract with Whitsons Culinary Group before reconsidering and approving a one-year renewal. Meanwhile, the Community Preservation Committee reviewed revised plans for Fayville Memorial Park and addressed a potential $350,000 funding shortfall for Phase 2 of the Peninsula Trail.

highlights.title: Regional emergency dispatch borrowing authorization
highlights.why: The Select Board approved up to $12.5 million in short-term borrowing to provide cash flow for construction of the regional emergency communications facility between state grant disbursements.

highlights.title: Joint Route 9 and I-495 corridor study support
highlights.why: The Planning Board voted 4-0 to endorse a joint One Stop for Growth grant application with Westborough to fund a $150,000 planning study focused on zoning, infrastructure, and residential neighborhood buffers.

highlights.title: Food service contract renewal approved on reconsideration
highlights.why: After concerns over food quality and staff morale led to an initial 3-4-2 failure, the committee voted 8-1 on reconsideration to approve a one-year contract extension with Whitsons Culinary Group to ensure cafeteria operations continue in the fall.

highlights.title: Fayville Memorial Park layout and parking revisions
highlights.why: Recreation officials presented community feedback that reduced the proposed splash pad to 2,000 square feet and moved it near the playground to protect sledding space, while an upcoming parking study will inform a revised grant application.

highlights.title: Peninsula Trail Phase 2 budget gap
highlights.why: Estimated costs for the Phase 2 bridge and boardwalk have risen to over $600,000 against $211,000 in existing funds, leading the Trails Committee to consider an upland trail route around wetlands to avoid boardwalk expenses.
